item.title: Shopify Expands Catalog Access to AI Agents for Automated Shopping and Checkout
item.description:
Shopify Expands Catalog Access to AI Agents for Automated Shopping and Checkout

Shopify announced Tuesday it will allow shoppers to configure AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving these agents access to a catalog of over a billion listings. This development marks an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions, moving beyond a previous exclusive partnership with Meta’s Muse agent. Users can now utilize any AI agent for browsing and purchasing without a specific partnership integration.

🔍 Overview

Shopify is marketing the new feature as a “personal shopper” that can act on a human’s behalf. The agent has access to a catalog consisting of items located both on and off Shopify storefronts. This move follows an earlier partnership announced in September with Meta to allow the Muse agent to browse and purchase items.

🧩 How it works

To enable automated shopping, customers must connect an AI agent to their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform designed to consolidate orders and track packages.

  • Integration: The agent connects directly to the user’s Shop account.
  • Checkout: Transactions occur via the one-click Shop Pay feature within the conversation with the agent.
  • Order Management: Any orders placed by the agent are funneled back to the Shop app for tracking.

⚙️ Key details

Humans remain in control of the agent’s behavior through specific rules and required authorizations:

  • Budget Guardrails: Users can set spending limits for the agent.
  • Shipping Preferences: Users can instruct agents to only display products with fast shipping.
  • Purchase Approval: Buyers are required to approve each purchase before it is finalized.

💡 Why it matters

E-commerce has emerged as a significant battleground for AI development, with companies like Google and Amazon also investing in tools where the end goal is an autonomous agent purchasing items for users. This shift has also sparked conflict between major commerce players and AI companies, such as the ongoing dispute between Amazon and firms like Perplexity and Meta over whether agents should be permitted to shop on a customer’s behalf.

#Shopify #AIagents #ECommerce #ShopPay #AgenticCommerce

Source: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents

item.title: Reactiv uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to automate Shopify app updates
item.description:
Reactiv uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to automate Shopify app updates

Reactiv has updated its mobile commerce product by implementing an AI Scheduler to autonomously update merchant apps on a schedule. By utilizing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Reactiv reduced merchant configuration time by 80 percent and reached production 33 percent faster.

🔍 Overview

Reactiv provides Shopify merchants with native iOS and Android apps, which see shopper conversion rates 2–4 times higher than web visitors. Their toolset includes analytics dashboards, a low-code app builder, and AI-powered features.

🧩 How it works

Reactiv built the AI Scheduler as a three-agent system using the Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The system consists of:

  • Supervisor: Classifies intent.
  • Analytics Agent: Queries merchant data.
  • Builder Agent: Generates configurations.

Reactiv packages its Strands agent graph as a Docker image, pushes it to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR), and deploys it to AgentCore. The system later unified interactive and scheduled agents onto a single stack to achieve shared memory across both modes.

⚙️ Key details

Reactiv migrated its configuration schema server (the Config MCP) from Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime. The MCP operates as a stateful server that initializes the current app configuration at the start of a session, with the Builder Agent performing mutations validated against the schema on every call.

Component Function
AgentCore runtime Handles managed agent execution
AgentCore memory Provides persistent cross-session context
AgentCore Identity Handles service-to-service authentication
Amazon EventBridge Provides Cron scheduling
Amazon Bedrock Provides foundation model access and guardrails

Memory and Isolation

AgentCore provides long-term memory scoped per merchant to maintain data privacy, utilizing three specific mechanisms:

  • Session summarizer: Condenses job actions into context for future runs.
  • Preference learner: Tracks merchant approvals or rejections of layouts over time.
  • Semantic fact extractor: Stores knowledge regarding brand guidelines, top sellers, and product categories.

Infrastructure isolation is managed via Firecracker microVMs, ensuring each merchant’s agent state, memory, and execution context runs in its own isolated environment.

#AmazonBedrock #Shopify #AIAgents #Ecommerce #AWS

Source: How Reactiv automates mobile commerce 80% faster with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Shopify Returns to Swift and Kotlin Codebases for Native Apps
item.description:
Shopify Returns to Swift and Kotlin Codebases for Native Apps

Shopify is moving from React Native back to separate Swift and Kotlin codebases for its native applications.

💡 Why it matters

In 2020, Shopify switched to React Native for three reasons:

  • Stop building the same features twice
  • Allow developers to work across the stack
  • Spend less time chasing feature parity and more time shipping value

Shopify states that agents can now handle enough of the implementation, translation, testing, and review work that those factors are no longer the deciding factors they were in 2020.

⚙️ Key details

Shopify is the maintainer of three significant React Native libraries. Their status is as follows:

Library Status
react-native-skia Finding a new home
flash-list Finding a new home
restyle To be archived at the end of 2026 (noted as having a smaller user base than other libraries)

#Shopify #ReactNative #Swift #Kotlin #AIagents

Source: Native is now the future of mobile at Shopify
